stem: The Period 3 elements show trends in physical and chemical properties across the period.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Explain why the elements $\text{Na}$ to $\text{Al}$ are good electrical conductors.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why the elements $\text{P}$, $\text{S}$ and $\text{Cl}$ do not conduct electricity.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Fig. 2.1 shows the variation in melting point of the Period 3 elements $\text{Si}$ to $\text{Cl}$.

{{figure:figure_2_1.png}}

The Period 3 elements $\text{Si}$ to $\text{Cl}$ are all non-metals.

Explain why there is a large difference between the melting point of $\text{Si}$ and the melting points of $\text{P}$, $\text{S}$ and $\text{Cl}$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Table 2.1 gives some information about some Period 3 chlorides.

Row B refers to the pH of the solution that forms when the Period 3 chloride is added to water.

Table 2.1

|  | formula of Period 3 chloride | $\text{NaCl}$ | $\text{MgCl}_2$ | $\text{AlCl}_3$ | $\text{SiCl}_4$ | $\text{PCl}_5$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| A | oxidation number of element bonded to $\text{Cl}$ |  |  |  |  |  |
| B | pH of solution |  | 6.5 |  |  |  |
| C | bonding |  |  | ionic |  |  |
| D | structure |  |  | giant |  |  |

Complete Table 2.1.

You may use the following abbreviations.

I = ionic, C = covalent, M = metallic
G = giant, S = simple

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Write an equation for the formation of $\text{AlCl}_3$ from its elements.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Write an equation for the formation of $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ from $\text{PCl}_5$.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.stem:
$\text{S}_2\text{Cl}_2\text{(l)}$ reacts with $\text{Cl}_2\text{(g)}$ in a reversible reaction to form $\text{SCl}_2\text{(l)}$. Under certain conditions, a dynamic equilibrium is established.

$$\text{S}_2\text{Cl}_2\text{(l)} + \text{Cl}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SCl}_2\text{(l)} \qquad \Delta H = -41\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$
parts.text: State what is meant by dynamic equilibrium.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: Identify the condition necessary to establish dynamic equilibrium.

parts.label: (e)(iii)
parts.text:
$\text{S}_2\text{Cl}_2\text{(l)}$ is yellow and $\text{SCl}_2\text{(l)}$ is red.

$$\text{S}_2\text{Cl}_2\text{(l)} + \text{Cl}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SCl}_2\text{(l)} \qquad \Delta H = -41\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

State what is observed when the following changes are made to an equilibrium mixture of $\text{S}_2\text{Cl}_2\text{(l)}$ and $\text{SCl}_2\text{(l)}$.

Explain your answers.

- The equilibrium mixture is warmed gently.

- The overall pressure of the equilibrium mixture is increased.

parts.label: (f)(i)
parts.stem: Aqueous $\text{MgCl}_2$ reacts with aqueous $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ to form a white precipitate. Upon heating, the white precipitate undergoes thermal decomposition.
parts.text: Construct an equation to show the reaction of aqueous $\text{MgCl}_2$ with aqueous $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$. Use state symbols in your equation.

parts.label: (f)(ii)
parts.text: Identify the products of the thermal decomposition of the white precipitate.

parts.label: (f)(iii)
parts.text: State the trend in thermal stability of the Group 2 carbonates down the group.
